title: Resilience, caching, and messaging — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: Prevent duplicate charges when a dependency times out. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What does a circuit breaker do?

options.text: Temporarily stops calls after failure conditions

questions.explanation: It limits calls to an unhealthy dependency according to a policy.

questions.prompt: What must at-least-once message consumers expect?
questions.explanation: Duplicate handling is part of the consumer contract.

questions.prompt: Why store a processed marker and business effect in one transaction?

options.text: To avoid marking success without the effect or applying it twice after a partial commit

questions.explanation: Atomic recording connects deduplication to the effect.

questions.prompt: What does a cache TTL define?

options.text: A guarantee the source never changes
How long an entry is considered usable under the cache policy

questions.explanation: TTL is a freshness policy, not proof of current source data.

questions.prompt: What problem can retries at several layers cause?

options.text: Multiplicative load on a failing dependency

questions.prompt: Does the sample HashSet deduplication survive a process restart?
questions.explanation: Durability requires persistent state and an atomic effect policy.
add succeeds; accepted becomes 1. add returns false; accepted stays 1. add succeeds; accepted becomes 2. This in-memory demo is single-threaded and not durable.
